title: Lightness: short kind lines shown after a logged session (AikiField issue #110)
status: Draft. No line is approved yet.
written_by: Claude (AI draft), in the style of the book-launch voice notes
license: Original text written for AikiField. No line is copied from a joke site, forum or book.

approval.how: Send a one-way notice, then add a 10-minute 'lightness sign-off' block to the Richard Session agenda. He accepts, rewrites or rejects each line. Set approved to true on the keepers.
approval.attribution: Lines are shown unattributed. They are not quotes from Richard or from anyone else.

display.note: Set show_unapproved to false to hide every line that is not approved yet.

guidelines: Warm, and never at anyone's expense.
No jokes about pain, injury, trauma, bodies, age or illness. No health claims.
No invented quotes from real people, and no real person's name in a line.
Physics is only a playful echo of the practice: recognition, never derivation.
Invitation, not instruction. Short bursts that circle back as questions.
Plain ASCII text, 220 characters or fewer.

kinds.twist: A short line with a turn in it.
kinds.question: Circles back to the player as a question.
kinds.self-mock: Laughs gently at the practitioner in all of us, never at one person.
kinds.scene: A tiny scene or a personified thing (a guest, laundry, a tide).
kinds.echo: A playful echo of physics. The practice came first; the physics is only a nod.
kinds.invite: A gentle invitation with a smile.

items.text: DropBackSinkOpen takes thirty seconds. Remembering to do it takes a lifetime of thirty seconds.
The reactive moment arrives uninvited. You do not have to give it the good chair.
Re-tightened already? Wonderful. That is one more chance to let go, and it cost nothing.
Your shoulders will climb back up. Be polite and drop them again. They are persistent, not malicious.
You cannot drop back from somewhere you are not. Have you checked where you are standing?
A fixed idea is just tension with perfect attendance. Outlast it, one finer release at a time.
Do not take the breath. Wait for it. It is the one thing in your day that has never once been late.
Counting the seconds until the breath arrives is timing, not waiting. Different sport. Which one are you playing?
Let it breathe you. It has done the job your whole life and never once asked for a review.
The wait for the impulse teaches patience. The breath has been waiting for you to stop managing it.
Locate your central core. Hint: it wandered off while you read the instructions. It comes back when asked nicely.
Move your attention one inch to the left and you live in a new neighborhood. No moving truck required.
Feel, locate, align, unify, stand there. Standing there turns out to be the advanced technique.
The glow of life has no off switch. It just has a lot of laundry piled in front of it.
Tense everything. Now release. Notice how much of 'everything' was optional.
Tensing the whole body on purpose: the one assignment where trying too hard counts as following directions.
How long should the scan take? As long as you are enjoying it. Overachievers, this is the trap. Walk in anyway.
Closer to the spine each time. When did anyone last ask the spine for its opinion?
Mind comes first on the list. It assumes this is a promotion.
Forehead, eyes, jaw, throat, shoulders: so many places to set things down. Who packed all of this?
Gravity has been holding you up all day for free. Sink into its shadow and say thanks.
No fixed pace. Your feet, at the end of the list, have been patient since breakfast.
Resist the push and they pull you. Resist the pull and they push you. Resist nothing and, annoyingly, you are still standing.
From fifty percent ground to sixty. The best news in the world, delivered in a very small number.
Your partner pushes, you wobble, they smile. The wobble is the lesson. Say thank you.
Resist, and a wrist grab becomes an argument. Nobody has ever been grounded by an argument.
If you can feel the resistance inside and they cannot see it outside, congratulations: you are getting worse at being obvious.
An invisible partner never pushes too hard. This is also why they teach so little. Buy a real one lunch.
All your cells are quietly enjoying the glow. Are you coming to the party?
Aiki Kokyu: the art of breathing with the room instead of at it.
Breathing in harmony is mostly matching the tempo of everything else. The tide has never rushed.
Air in, oxygen across, blood onward, cells absorbing, life burning. Five stages, one breath, zero committee meetings.
Reverse the imagery and you are promoted from breather to breathed. No extra paperwork.
The lungs run the front desk. The cells do the actual work. Both deserve a thank-you note.
Somewhere in there a tiny delivery service has run all day without a single tip. Breathe a little thanks.
Debt, saturation, reserve. Not a bank statement, but where is your balance today?
Two or three breaths, exactly the way you want. The only exam where you wrote the answer key.
It usually takes fewer than three and never takes seven. If you are on breath eight, you have graduated to simply breathing.
Your own mask first. This is not selfish. It is the only way anyone else's mask ever gets on.
You can breathe at the ocean even when you cannot be there. The ocean is very understanding about this.
The imaginary ocean has one great feature: no sand in the sandwiches.
Remember the first breath of sea air. Your cells do, and they will happily do it again for free.
An infant has never checked whether it was breathing correctly. Has anyone complained?
Three minutes of breathing like someone who has never heard of an inbox.
Lie there, breathe, enjoy the glow. The one exercise where being hopeless at productivity is the whole assignment.
Rate your state from one to ten. Notice how often the honest answer is 'a five, but I will say fine.'
Call up the next number and embody it. Eight arrives faster when you ask politely. Did you say please?
Dropping a number back is not rehearsing a bad day. It is a guided tour of the neighborhood you are moving out of.
Ten is the number that does not take calls.
Plateau: the only kind of stuck where you get to choose the altitude. How high today?
A ten with an agenda is a seven wearing a costume.
Enjoying yourself enjoying joy is a circle with no corners. Unless you start grading it.
Feeling better is guidance, not a prize. You cannot lose it, only forget to check. Checked lately?
Joy does not need a meeting to get started. What happens when nobody schedules one?
Close with DBSO. Even joy appreciates a clean landing.
Early, late, or close? Your partner will answer with the honesty usually reserved for restaurant reviews.
Do not telegraph. If your face announced it, the surprise left before you did.
Snap your fingers the instant you sense it coming: the world's smallest applause for noticing in time.
Face the attacker so you can feel their attention. Yes, staring is allowed. Yes, it is also practice.
Climb a few octaves, then replay the meeting. Suddenly it has better manners. Whose, exactly?
Push past the satisfying strategy for a quantum shift. Think of it as ordering dessert after you said you were full.
The upcoming situation has not read your visualization yet. Send it a gentle copy.
KeepDoingIt is not thrilling advice. That is the secret. Were you expecting fireworks?
Nobody has ever finished breathing. Therefore: KeepDoingIt.
The art is not never wobbling. It is the speed of your 'oh, there I am.'
A wobble noticed is a wobble halfway home. Which half are you in?
Energy follows attention. This explains where it goes at night: the refrigerator.
Reactions are an inside job. The traffic is just the stage crew.
The pause before replying is a trainable skill. The reply-all button has not been informed.
Presence is a practice, so you will be wonderfully bad at it on days that end in Y.
The only way to be late for the present is to arrive early with a plan.
Thank your partner. They do all the falling and get none of the credit.
Every partner is unwilling at least once. That is when the lesson pulls up a chair.
Most arguments run on a lot of resistance and a little listening. Try the recipe the other way round, once, for fun.
The floating bridge of heaven is easy to stand on. Finding the stairs is the practice.
Waves do not ask whether you are ready. Surfers have simply stopped taking it personally.
Physics keeps finding new words for what the mat already knew.
Everything is a wave until somebody checks. Consider checking a little less.
Wave or particle? It depends who is watching. This is also true of your Tuesday.
A quantum leap is, technically, the smallest jump there is. Ever finer increments, everyone.
The unified field: one big room, no assigned seating.
Joy, once noticed, tends to bring friends.
Beautiful world, small print: you go first.
You do not need more time to breathe. The next one is already on the calendar. Attending?
Be a beginner on purpose. The view is better and nobody expects you to know where anything is.
Same notes, different smile. That is most of jazz, and most of practice.
The unknown has excellent hospitality and terrible signage. Shall we go in anyway?
Take yourself lightly. It is the one weight you get to choose. What did you pick today?
Practice report: showed up, forgot everything, remembered. That is the whole syllabus.
Your attention gets lent out all day. Calling it home counts as practice. Where is it right now?
Gravity is the original teacher. Zero tuition, perfect attendance.
A deep breath is just an ordinary breath that finally got noticed.
The center is not far. It is merely excellent at hide-and-seek and terrible at hiding. Getting warmer?
Missed a day? The practice kept your seat. It is not the sort to take attendance.
The progress dots fill in only when you do. A fair system, and a patient one.
Mr. Hyde has one weakness. He cannot stand a good pause.
Energy is the price of admission to anything new. Lunch is a perfectly respectable ticket booth.
Aiki-land has no border guards. The only sign says, 'You are already here.'
The original character for ki is a picture of steam. This explains why the best ideas keep arriving in the shower.
Learning out loud: being wrong, with better acoustics.
